title: Grateful Dead Live at Nassau Veterans Memorial Coliseum on 1973-03-16
lineage: Dat (Sony R500) -> SEK'D Prodif Plus -> Samplitude Professional -> FLAC
source: Set 1: SBD -> Master Reel -> PCM -> Dat (44.1k) DSet 2: SBD -> Master Reel -> Cassette -> Dat (44.1k) D

ai_review.summary: A crisp Charlie Miller sound‑board capture of a classic March 16, 1973 Nassau show, highlighted by a soaring Dark Star, stellar Bird Song and a monster Playing in the Band.
ai_review.review: The SBD transfer is generally clean and well‑balanced, though a few listeners note occasional clipping from hot board levels that eases in the second set. Musically the performance shines – the first‑set China > Rider opener, Jack Straw and an inspired Bird Song set the tone, while the second set delivers Promised Land → Bertha → Greatest, a powerful Dark Star that flows into Truckin' → Morning Dew. Overall it’s regarded as a solid, energetic 1973 show with several standout jams.

ai_rating.rationale: The majority of reviews are 4‑5 stars and praise both the performance and sound quality; weighting musical merit (70%) with solid recording (30%) yields a high overall rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, clean mastering praised by many; some comments about hot board levels causing clipping early in the set, but overall listenable and well balanced.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set builds nicely with China>Rider opener and strong mid‑set numbers; second set kicks off with a powerful Promised Land suite, delivers a memorable Dark Star that segues into Truckin' and a heartfelt Morning Dew, making for an energetic and cohesive two‑set performance.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar tone described as perfect and his solos on Dark Star and Playing in the Band were highlighted as electrifying.
band_member_comments.Phil: Lesh is repeatedly called "smoking" with strong bass lines and notable backing vocals throughout the show.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir receives praise for solid rhythm work and vocal performances, especially on songs like Ramble On Rose and Bird Song.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith’s piano/keyboard contributions are noted as excellent, adding depth to transitions and jams in both sets.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann’s drumming is described as great and solid, driving the energy of the set, especially on Truckin' and the Dark Star.
